Nema for Product

Turn customer conversations into product context.

Nema brings selected customer evidence and prior decisions into a product thread as a reviewable brief. Product managers can see the patterns, outliers, and unanswered questions before choosing a direction.

All teams ↗

Keep the customer evidence attached

Product teams hear the same feature phrase from sales, support, research, and customer success, but the underlying need can differ. Nema can collect a selected set of conversations and build a theme brief with every example linked to its source.

The result gives PMs a faster way to inspect evidence without flattening it. A frequent request, a severe problem, and a strategic opportunity are different signals. Nema prepares the material; the product team decides what it means and whether it should affect the roadmap.

Synthesize feedback without losing outliers

Start with a defined set of records, a time window, and the customer question you want to understand. Ask Nema to group statements by customer job, describe meaningful differences within each group, and preserve minority views that challenge the main pattern.

A useful brief lists the theme, linked examples, affected context, and open questions. It can flag requests that sound similar but describe different workflows. The PM can then choose follow-up interviews, check product data, or decide that the sample is too narrow.

Prepare a discovery decision

Combine approved research notes, customer threads, relevant metrics, and earlier product decisions. Nema can draft a discovery brief with the current evidence, tensions, assumptions, and open questions. Ask it to show which claims come from observed behavior and which come from team interpretation.

This makes a review meeting more focused. The team can debate the unresolved points instead of rebuilding the source history. Product leadership still sets the hypothesis, research plan, and decision standard.

Bring context into backlog intake

When a Slack thread should become an issue, Nema can find possible related work and prepare a draft with the customer problem, evidence, reproduction details where relevant, and links back to the conversation. It should describe possible duplicates as candidates for review.

The product owner chooses whether to create the issue, how to frame it, and where it belongs. Priority, scope, and commitment stay out of the automated draft. If the issue is created through a connected app, the exact title and body should be visible first.

Draft release context from shipped work

Give Nema a confirmed release list, the product decision behind each change, and the intended audience. It can draft outcome-led release notes that explain what changed using only completed evidence.

This keeps internal implementation details out of customer copy and avoids describing merged work as deployed. Product and engineering owners verify the release state and approve the final language.

Start with one feedback question

Choose five to ten records containing related but nonidentical requests. Ask for a theme brief and check whether every statement has a valid link, important differences remain visible, and no priority appears by implication. Add other sources only after the first synthesis helps the PM decide what to investigate.

Questions from product teams

Does Nema prioritize the roadmap?

No. Nema prepares evidence, themes, and open questions. Product managers set priority using strategy, impact, effort, and judgment.

Can Nema create issues in our tracker?

When that connection and action are available, Nema can propose an issue for review. The product owner approves its content and destination.

How are sources preserved?

Ask Nema to attach a link or citation to each example and keep the original record in its owning system. The brief should make it easy to return to the source.
